summary.headline: Mayur Uniquoters Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 18% to INR282.95 crore and PAT 42% to INR57.99 crore, helped by warehouse stock clearance in the US.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR282.95 crore (up 18% YoY), with PBT of INR79.31 crore (up 43%) and PAT of INR57.99 crore (up 42%). Standalone revenue was INR252.99 crore (up 6%), with PBT of INR70.46 crore (up 9%) and PAT of INR51.27 crore (up 7%). Management attributed the consolidated outperformance to lower dispatches from India and higher sales from the US warehouse, which cleared its own stock. Export OEM volumes were weak YoY because US auto demand softened, though management said orders are in hand and the trend is improving. Management declined to give formal guidance for the second half or FY28, and the Executive Director was absent from the call due to a family bereavement.

financial_highlights.value: INR90.46 crore (General INR33 crore; OEM INR57.46 crore)
OEM INR62.80 crore; Replacement INR45.02 crore; Footwear INR45.34 crore; Furnishing INR7.19 crore; Others INR2.18 crore; Domestic total INR162.53 crore

financial_highlights.change: Lower QoQ due to Q1 labour-code provision reversal in Q2

segments.name: Export OEM (standalone)
segments.commentary: INR57.46 crore in Q2, below the INR75-80 crore run-rate cited by an analyst; management said it is improving. Volumes were up 13.5% YoY and 5% QoQ, though the export volume YoY was negative per management.

segments.name: Export General
segments.commentary: INR33 crore in Q2. Management expects double-digit improvement, supported by a newly started retail arm in Europe.

segments.name: Domestic auto replacement
segments.commentary: INR45.02 crore in Q2. Volume grew about 11% QoQ and about 5% YoY.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: INR45.34 crore in Q2. Management said volume and value both rose, and guided to 5-10% annual volume growth. Focus is on selected, higher-margin customers.

segments.name: Furnishing
segments.commentary: INR7.19 crore in Q2. Retail is facing price competition; about 750-800 sub-dealers and 8-10 distributors were appointed.

segments.name: PU (polyurethane)
segments.commentary: Revenue booked INR6.28 crore in Q2. Management said the segment is not profitable and operates at about 25% utilisation versus about 40% needed for breakeven.

guidance_outlook: Export OEM expected at INR250-300 crore in FY27 (consolidated basis), versus about INR260-280 crore in FY26 after a confused exchange on the figure.
Export OEM expected to return to INR75-80 crore per quarter from the current level, with improvement described as gradual rather than dated.
Gross margin sustainable at about 55-56%, with variation tied to raw material and crude prices.
No guidance given for H2 FY27 or FY28 top-line or bottom-line; management said the current margin should hold and top-line growth around 20% should continue.
Export OEM expected to grow 10-15% in the following two years, per management.
capex_capacity: New machinery for an additional line: equipment expected in late November to December 2026, installation to begin in the March 2027 quarter, with operations starting in Q1 FY28.
A new plant in India is under consideration, especially in the South region; a Mexico plant is in the pipeline but not concluded.
Capacity utilisation is unchanged QoQ; PU business is at about 25% utilisation against about 40% needed for breakeven.
Bhadla mini-grid solar investment: management cited a payback period of at most 2 years.
demand_pricing: US auto demand weak for two quarters; OEMs revised projections and Q2 US dispatches were deliberately reduced, with warehouse stock cleared instead.
US OEM orders expanded to 5 models from 2 for Ford and Chrysler; BMW and Mercedes-Benz (export OEM) are taking material close to full projections.
Freight and PVC costs spiked from the West Asia conflict and are now easing; management will not pass costs to export customers until increases look stable and permanent.
Footwear and furnishing domestic markets face high price competition; management is deprioritising footwear in favour of higher-margin auto exports.
Pipeline includes VW, plus leather accessories talks in the Kolkata and Kanpur belt; management said new OEM wins take 2-3 years to convert.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of export and domestic auto OEM volume growth, and reasons for weak export volumes.
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic replacement volume grew about 11% QoQ and 5% YoY; OEM volume grew 13.5% YoY and 5% QoQ. Export volume was negative YoY because US customers delayed new car purchases; the warehouse cleared its own stock.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost and other income fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 had an extra provision for labour-code changes that was reversed in Q2, so underlying employee cost is about INR12.5 crore per quarter. Other income fell QoQ due to fair-value losses on treasury investments; YoY it rose.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin sustainability given volatility (Q1 about 52%, Q2 about 57%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to about 55-56% as sustainable, with variation driven by raw material and crude prices.

qa_highlights.question: Transfer pricing between India and the US warehouse subsidiary.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the subsidiary keeps the margin needed to cover its local costs and the rest is billed to the subsidiary. Example given: a 10% margin split 8% India and 2% US subsidiary. When consolidated revenue exceeds standalone, the consolidated margin is higher.

qa_highlights.question: Export OEM size and FY26 base: analyst cited INR285-290 crore.
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said about INR200 crore for FY26, then about INR260 crore, then confirmed about INR280 crore on a consolidated basis, with FY27 expected at INR250-300 crore. The numbers were inconsistent on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Succession planning after the AGM resolution was not passed.
qa_highlights.answer: The board discussed it; the resolution will be re-proposed with a revised structure after the remuneration and perquisite terms were objected to. A third generation joined about 6 months ago, but Manav Poddar is not directly running the business at present.

risks_watch: Export OEM recovery depends on US OEM schedules; the Q2 export volume decline YoY was attributed to customers delaying new car purchases.
Consolidated growth was flattered by warehouse stock clearance; watch whether standalone growth catches up in Q3 and Q4.
PU segment remains loss-making at about 25% utilisation, with breakeven at about 40%; tax benefits are masking the loss.
Inconsistent export OEM figures given on the call (INR200 crore, INR260 crore, INR280 crore) need reconciliation in the next disclosure.
Governance: AGM resolution not passed and must be re-tabled; Executive Director absent from call; succession still open.
Gross margin is volatile, tied to crude and raw material prices; freight and PVC costs may rebound.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the US/South Africa OEM pipeline, but evasive on forward numbers: no guidance for H2 FY27 or FY28, and several figures (export OEM base, transfer pricing) were corrected or left unclear during Q&A.
key_quotes: Basically, market is not responding well in U.S. for last 2 quarters.
So the sale, which increased is because of clearance of the stock from warehouse and in comparison to dispatch from India.
PU, it's not, in fact, generating profit just -- but we are managing because of some tax benefits and all.

adds.what: New machinery for an additional production line (equipment late Nov-Dec 2026; installation from Mar 2027 quarter)

growth.why: Management gave no formal H2 FY27 or FY28 guidance; it cited FY27 Export OEM INR250-300 crore and said top-line growth around 20% should continue, but Q2 consolidated growth was flattered by one-off US warehouse stock clearance while standalone grew only 6%, and the new line only goes live in Q1 FY28 with PU at 25% utilisation.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin rose to about 57% in Q2 from about 52% in Q1 and management guided a sustainable 55-56%, though it is tied to crude and raw material prices, and gross margin at the consolidated level is flattered by the US subsidiary mix.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New machinery for an additional line is being delivered Nov-Dec 2026, installation from the March 2027 quarter, with operations starting Q1 FY28, though PU runs at about 25% utilisation against about 40% needed for breakeven.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Export OEM FY27 is guided at INR250-300 crore and footwear volume at 5-10% a year, with export OEM volume up 13.5% YoY and 5% QoQ, but export volume was negative YoY and standalone revenue grew only 6%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: A new plant in India (South region) is under consideration and a Mexico plant is in the pipeline but not concluded, while utilisation is low at about 25% in PU, so the case for a new plant is weaker than the case for the line already being added.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal guidance was given for H2 FY27 or FY28, and the Q2 consolidated beat of 18% was flattered by a one-off US warehouse stock clearance while standalone grew only 6%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Export OEM run-rate of about INR57.46 crore in Q2 is well below the INR75-80 crore per quarter needed for the FY27 range, and the US auto demand softness has persisted for two quarters.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A newly started retail arm in Europe supports export general, and leather accessories and VW pipeline talks are ongoing, but new OEM wins take 2-3 years to convert.

rows.label: US OEM model expansion (Ford, Chrysler)
rows.why: US OEM orders expanded to 5 models from 2 for Ford and Chrysler, and BMW and Mercedes-Benz are taking material close to full projections, though US customers delayed new car purchases in Q2.

rows.label: Pass-through of freight and PVC cost increases
rows.why: Management will not pass freight and PVC cost increases to export customers until they look stable and permanent, and these costs are currently easing after the West Asia spike.

rows.label: Succession and AGM resolution re-tabling
rows.why: The AGM resolution was not passed on remuneration and perquisite terms and will be re-proposed with a revised structure, while Manav Poddar is not yet running the business.

tone.note: Management was confident on gross margin (about 57% in Q2, guided 55-56%) and on the US OEM pipeline, but gave no H2 FY27 or FY28 guidance and the export OEM base figures (INR200, 260, 280 crore) were inconsistent, which analysts pressed on along with the Q2 export OEM shortfall against the INR75-80
